title: alkanna graeca subsp. baeotica
intro: Alkanna graeca subsp. baeotica, commonly known as Greek alkanna, is a plant species belonging to the borage family (Boraginaceae). It is traditionally used in folk medicine for its anti-inflammatory, antiseptic, and antipyretic properties, making it beneficial for treating various health conditions such as wounds, fever, and gastrointestinal issues. The therapeutic actions of Greek alkanna include reducing inflammation, preventing bacterial growth, and alleviating pain. The plant's bioactive constituents include alkaloids, flavonoids, and saponins, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
